speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness, can you tell me if your symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The symptoms you describe—double vision when looking up/down, limb weakness worsening with activity, and improvement with rest—strongly suggest a specific neuromuscular condition. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis) or difficulty swallowing?

REQUEST TEST: Electrodiagnostic_Studies (EMG/Nerve_Conduction)
REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receiver_Antibody_Titer

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electrodiagnostic_Studies (EMG/Nerve_Conduction): Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; Acetylcholine_Receiver_Antibody_Titer: Present (elevated)

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The pattern of fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest, combined with ocular symptoms like double vision, is classic for this condition despite the mention of tuberculosis; the latter appears to be a misinterpretation by a previous provider.
